story_text.value:
Been working on a quantitative trading platform for 3~ years, at first 2.5 years off and on, then full-time for the last eight months when agents became capable. I started using agents seriously after writing 30K lines of code and found an agentic workflow I could trust, and I turned that workflow into Pullboard. So, this holds up in real systems.

Essential Loop:

claim -> build -> verify (different agent reviews, see website.)

Primitive Concepts:

https://pullboard.dev/tutorials/

What makes this workflow valuable is the "Agentic Institutional Knowledge" built up over time outside the codebase in the Pullboard history; e.g., items, shouts and doctrine all get referenced, discussed and those lessons remain available to future agents instead of disappearing into chats. The best part is I hardly re-explain myself.

You do have to steer agents and make decisions, but this is quite nearly autonomous development. Anyways it is early and open source. Feedback welcome. Thank you!!

title.value: Show HN: Pullboard – An agent workflow for serious projects

story_text.value:
Hi HN!

I'm Ryan, I'm building Higherlevel (https://higherlevel.to) so product teams have one place to define and review software changes.

Over the last couple of years, I've been increasingly delegating software implementation to AI coding agents.

However, because it became easier and faster to ship complexity, I realised that it still takes me quite some time to even understand what the software is doing, why it is doing that, or review the changes.

I also don't do traditional code reviews anymore, it's mostly automated but I still want to review the final outcome of the changes (rather than its implementation).

I regularly work on complex B2B applications where a single feature can involve dozen of business rules, edge cases and interactions with existing functionality.

I found myself spending more and more time discovering and explaining requirements to agents, reviewing their output, asking for evdience and trying to establish whether we actually agreed on what correct behaviour looked like.

So I built Higherlevel. The idea is to bring product specifications and proof of work into a single collaborative workspace.

You can: - describe the current behaviour, known limitations and expected changes - define business rules, acceptance scenarios using Given/When/Then - demand evidence in the form of a screenshot, a video, etc - comment directly on the spec, on a specific area of the image or a timestamp of the video - discuss changes, track revisions and approve results with your team

I've written extensively about why I believe in specification driven development (and what it means to me) here https://higherlevel.to/blog/introducing-higherlevel

Higherlevel is currently in beta and built with Elixir, Phoenix LiveView, and PostgreSQL.

title.value: Show HN: Higherlevel – Define and review what AI agents build

story_text.value:
COOL + ALPHABETS = COOLPHABETS

COOLPHABETS teaches you to read and write in your mother tongue - for kids who are just starting, and adults who never did.

Millions of families live outside the country they were born in. While parents can read and write in their native language, their kids - the second generation - can barely do so.

Kids often speak their mother tongue fluently because it is the language they use at home. But reading and writing is rarely a "felt need" for them. And kids are unlikely to feel that need unless parents nudge them - preferably at an early age.

Many parents genuinely want their kids to be able to read and write in their mother tongue. This usually means a textbook or a weekend language class. Both can feel like a chore.

Most language apps teach you to 'speak' a language. COOLPHABETS teaches you to 'read' and 'write'. Reading and writing are a genuinely difficult problem to solve - especially on an app. Getting a child to write letters correctly is the harder part.

That's where we built CoolphaSense - a collection of tiny AI models that run entirely on the device and provide instant feedback on handwriting.

COOLPHABETS is designed for kids. No ads. No tracking. COPPA compliant. The apps are designed to work fully offline. No cloud roundtrips to a 'Mothership AI model'.

COOLPHABETS is currently available in Indian languages.

- Telugu - Kannada - Hindi - Tamil - Marathi

Most other Indian languages will be onboarded by December 2026. Other world languages (Asian, Middle Eastern, European) are early next year.

The bigger motivation is cultural. A language can survive for several generations as a spoken language, but if its script is lost, something important is lost with it. If one generation stops reading and writing in its native script, reconnecting with that part of the culture becomes much harder.

If you are a parent who feels this way, COOLPHABETS is for you and your kids.

https://coolphabets.com/

Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.coolphabet...

iPhone: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/coolphabets/id6762379998

We would love to hear from parents settled outside their native countries, parents raising kids in multilingual households, and from people working on handwriting recognition, on-device AI/ML, and language learning.

title.value: Show HN: Coolphabets – Teaching kids to read and write in their mother tongue

story_text.value:
Hi everyone,

When I first heard about WebMCP 6 weeks ago, I started thinking about what problems it might create. One question that came to mind was how developers would evaluate WebMCP tools and monitor them in production. That's when I decided to build Senro, a platform that helps devs test WebMCP tools using goal-oriented evals, trajectory evals, and more across LLMs, as well as monitor how those tools are used in production. Senro has a free plan (not a free trial). You can monitor up to 25K events/mo and run up to 250 evals/mo using your own API key (sorry, we're not venture-backed yet).

story_text.value:
Hi HN. There are lots of API gateways out there. What we couldn't find was one with everything built-in to go from “my business logic works” to “I can safely consider publishing it on the internet”. So we spent a year building the features in APIblaze: A serverless MCP and API gateway. Here’s what makes it different:

- Authorization. Most gateways stop at authentication: they check who is calling. What they can and cannot do is left to your code or a plugin connecting to some sort of complex Authorization system. APIblaze provides users & groups management and enforces Authorization policies at the gateway, as a default suggested from your API spec. You add groups and write Authorization rules in plain English ("only whoever created a record, or an admin, can read or change that record"), tested and enforced by the gateway.

- Hosted end to end. APIblaze hosts the MCP server, the gateway, OAuth discovery and the login pages on the internet. One thing we really wanted to make easy was local development so the hosted API gateway forwards the requests to your backend, even if this backend runs on your localhost. So you can connect Claude/ChatGPT/… to the hosted MCP, bring your own oAuth and log into it (which is important because MCPs are all about taking actions and you have to know “who” is taking those actions), chat with your API to test it, and change your code live while the calls stream in your terminal.

- UI widgets: self-service API keys, users and groups and chat window. A drop-in React widget lets your users create, rotate and revoke their own keys on the developer section of your site. Another lets your customers' admins manage their own users and groups. A last one lets end users chat with your API on your App.

- Multi-tenant. Each customer gets its own keys, users, portal and MCP address to serve their own service to their end-users.

- The usual gateway tools: rate limits and quotas, transformations, custom domains and more.

- No lock-in: one command exports your setup (config, users, groups, and API keys as hashes so your callers keep theirs) to a runnable Kong bundle once you outgrow APIblaze.

To try it, paste this prompt into Claude Code or Codex, in an empty folder (you get a sample app) or in your backend's folder:

> Show me what APIblaze does using npx apiblaze skills

Or by hand, no sign-up needed:

  npx apiblaze create --target https://ninopizzas.com/openapi.yaml
It's in beta. I'd love your feedback, what you like and what you don't.

title.value: Show HN: APIblaze – Serverless MCP and API gateway with everything built in

story_text.value:
Our background is trading systems and exchanges. Liquid Inference applies that to LLM inference. On Liquid Inference, model providers compete with each other on an open marketplace to offer the best price for any given model. We paired that with an intelligent auto-router so you always pay the lowest cost on the spot for a preset quality level.

Currently we're cheaper on Kimi/GPT/GLM but working hard to be the best price for all models.

You can also customize your minimum routing settings if you have particular requirements like what region the compute can be served from, zero data retention, provider/model allowlists, etc.

It's easy to set up, I usually just ask the harness itself to "write me a shell script to start Claude Code using Liquid Inference" for example and it just goes from there.

We're eager to hear your feedback!

title.value: Show HN: Liquid Inference – auto-routing to competitive LLM marketplace
